title: TRENDnet camera flaw exposed private live feeds without passwords
summary: A software flaw in TRENDnet SecurView internet cameras allowed people who knew a camera's internet address to view live video, and sometimes audio, without login credentials. The Federal Trade Commission said links to nearly 700 private camera feeds were posted online, including feeds showing children and activity inside homes. TRENDnet issued firmware updates, and the FTC later entered a final consent order requiring a security program and assessments.

key_claims: The FTC alleged that TRENDnet's security failures allowed unauthorized access to consumers' live camera feeds.
The complaint states that links to nearly 700 live feeds were posted online and that exposed feeds showed private activities inside homes.

sources.title: Critical Firmware Update: New IP Camera Firmware Eliminates Security Threat
key_claims: TRENDnet acknowledged that hackers could gain unauthorized access to affected SecurView IP-camera video feeds.
The company published firmware updates for affected cameras purchased between April 2010 and February 2012.

sources.title: Flaw in Home Security Cameras Exposes Live Feeds to Hackers
key_claims: WIRED independently reported that password-protected TRENDnet camera streams could be viewed by anyone who knew the camera address.

statutes_or_policies: Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act
FTC final consent order issued February 7, 2014

outcomes: TRENDnet released firmware updates for affected cameras.
The FTC's final order required a comprehensive information-security program, independent assessments every two years for 20 years, and consumer notice.

title: Wyze incident exposed camera thumbnails and videos across customer accounts
summary: After a February 16, 2024 service outage, Wyze's systems associated some camera-event data with the wrong customer accounts. Wyze said about 13,000 users received thumbnails from cameras that were not their own and 1,504 users opened those thumbnails; in some cases an attached event video was viewed. Wyze removed the caching library involved and added another verification layer between users and event videos.
